insightRRA.title: Regulatory reporting architecture: a resilient blueprint
insightRRA.lede: A pragmatic architecture for regulated environments: traceable ingestion, deterministic transformations, verifiable rules, and auditable outputs.

s1.title: Core goal
s1.body: Deliver correct regulatory outputs (TXT/XML/Excel) with full lineage: from source system to field-level evidence, including approvals and operational controls.

s2.title: Key layers
s2.li1: Ingestion & normalization: connectors + staging + canonical model
s2.li2: Validation: rule engine + thresholds + exceptions workflow
s2.li4: Auditability: evidence store, reproducibility, and immutable run logs

s3.title: Operational resilience
s3.body: Treat every report run as a controlled process: approvals, roles (owner/custodian/generator), idempotent runs, and post-run reconciliation checks.

insightMDR.title: Metadata-driven reporting: scale without rewriting
insightMDR.lede: Metadata separates business change from code change: mappings, validations, and output formats evolve without re-engineering the pipeline.

s1.title: What “metadata-driven” means
s1.body: Definitions live in data: report structure, field rules, source mappings, and output formatting. Code becomes a stable engine that interprets metadata.

s2.title: What you gain
s2.li1: Faster onboarding of new reports (reuse engine + define metadata)
s2.li2: Safer change management (versioned schemas and mappings)
s2.li3: Clear governance (who changed what, when, and why)
s2.li4: Consistent validations across institutions and formats

s3.title: Enterprise-grade controls
s3.body: Combine metadata with approvals, separation of duties, and an evidence trail so auditors can reproduce any report output deterministically.

cta.title: Recommended next step
cta.body: Create a small set of canonical metadata tables for one report (AN03) and grow from there: mappings → rules → outputs → audit.
